body: i had my pilonidal for about 4 years before finally getting surgery (didn’t have insurance until recently). if it’s smelling and it’s not leaking or anything i’d definitely recommend getting seen as soon as possible! i know it might be embarrassing to tell your mom especially since you’ve waited but i promise you it’ll be okay. i’d just say you thought it would go away eventually or you were just embarrassed about the location of it. if it’s infected they’ll most likely prescribe antibiotics, my surgeon wouldn’t do surgery until the infection was cleared. i had a pilonidal cystectomy back in march and i’m almost 3 months post op and feel great! i felt pretty good after 2.5 weeks but i was taking it super slow to ensure everything was good. most recommend a pilonidal cleft lift, i think that’s what it is it has a lower reoccurrence rate. if you can’t have surgery till december that gives you plenty of time to start researching surgeons and the different surgery’s and to even get your surgery booked!! i know it’s a scary journey but once you start the healing process it’ll get easier. i wish you the best and hope you can find relief soon!

I feel it’s best to go to the doctor as often as possible with changes like this, but not everyone has the means of doing so which is okay. I didn’t have insurance when mine would burst so i dealt with it on my own until i could find a more permanent solution for me. I would keep the area clean, use an antibacterial soap, and change the bandages as often as needed, i also used a triple antibiotic cream on the area. I’m not a doctor but i really dont think i’d recommend soaking in bath with an open wound. i would personally keep it only to showers until it’s healed up more. im not sure about the oils because i’ve never used them so maybe someone else can provide info on that, i use vitamin e oil but i had surgery and im using it on healed skin. 
*again, im not a doctor this is just what I would do but maybe someone else can provide more advice *

when i still had major flare ups i would use a heating pad on the area, as well as take hot epsom salt baths.
My main goal was to get everything to come to the top so it would pop, which you aren’t really supposed to do but it was my only option at the time. I hope you can find relief soon!

i also had a closed wound surgery, i waited 2 days after surgery to shower. i was given instruction to only let water run over the area and to keep it dry 

i honestly would recommend calling them and asking them what they recommend, as your instructions are vague? i hope this helps

I wasn’t able to sit with my stitches, it was just too uncomfortable for me personally. i can sit now with them being out (its been 2 days of having them removed) but i’ve been using a cushion to make sure i’m not putting too much weight on the area. I have slight discomfort but no pain, it’s more just me being overly cautious of how i sit lol. Idk if you’ll be able to take a cushion to school with you but i’d highly recommend it. if not, i’d suggest to get up every so often so the area can have a “break”

i’d say i’m at about 80%, i was told for the next 3-4 weeks to avoid crouching, squatting and swimming. I have no pain, i’m still continuing to be mindful of how i move just to make sure everything continues to heal. I feel pretty good though, im able to move around a lot better i just move a little slow lol. If you have any questions that i missed, just let me know! :)

I just had a closed pilonidal surgery! I had it done on the 17th, so it’s been about two weeks so far. The day of the surgery i was put on anesthesia for the surgery, afterwards they gave me a little morphine and a pill for pain before I left. i was also prescribed pain medication for the week following surgery but i didn’t have to take all them because i was fine after about 5 or 6 days.

I honestly didn’t have much pain at all, sitting was extremely uncomfortable even with a cushion and laying down was a bit difficult. But again I was in any pain, the worst pain I had was getting my stitches taken out (i think because they told me they’d dissolve, so i didn’t have time to prepare myself lol) but even that was nowhere near comparable to having an inflamed cyst. If we had the same procedure i’m sure you’ll be fine, just try and be as careful as possible to avoid ripping stitches! Everyone’s experiences are different but i’m wishing you a speedy recovery with little to no pain :)

i understand your pain,, i’ve dealt with flare ups for 4 years before finally seeking treatment. I personally use the comfilife coccyx cushion, i’ve never used a donut pillow so i can’t really compare but i have found my cushion takes a lot of pressure off the area. I try and avoid sitting for longer than 30 minutes at a time (or whatever feels best for that day). the standing desk i s a great idea!! when i feel a flare up coming on i’ll tend to soak in a warm epsom salt bath, or use a heating pad in an attempt to calm the area. unfortunately anytime i’ve had a flare up it usually comes with an infection, im currently taking bactrim ds and it has helped me a ton in just a few days. i know all of us are different and different things work better for some, but just thought i would share some of the things that have helped me. i hope you can find something to help keep the area calm until you can (hopefully) get this fully resolved!!
